# Add state-aware affordability filtering for storyline options

## Summary

Extend `getStorylineOptions` (or add a companion state-aware accessor) that filters out unaffordable options based on `cost` fields. Store the presented/available option list on `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Affordability filter.** `getAffordableOptions(state, event)` returns options where `cost` is affordable (coins and/or reputation gates checked). Options with no cost are always included.
- **Pending choice stores presented list.** `PendingEventChoice` gains an optional `presentedOptions: StorylineOption[]` field populated at choice-draw time.
- **Filtering is stable.** The presented list is computed once at draw and does not change during the pending choice period.
- **Backwards compatible.** Events with no cost-gated options return the same list as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `getAffordableOptions()`, update `createPendingStorylineChoice()` to populate `presentedOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `presentedOptions` to `PendingEventChoice`.

## Deliverables

- New/pure function `getAffordableOptions`.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice` populates `presentedOptions`.
- Unit tests for affordability filter.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — deterministic filtering.
data.title: Add affordability filtering to getStorylineOptions

# Deduct cost and apply extra effects during storyline option resolution

## Summary

At resolution time (`resolveStorylineOption` / `resolveEventOption`), deduct the option's `cost` from the player's resources and apply any `extraEffect` independently of the `effectPolicy`. This is the core gameplay change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost deduction.** When an affordable option is selected, its `cost.coins` (if set) and `cost.reputation` (if set) are deducted from `state.resourceBank`.
- **Extra effect application.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`. Both can coexist (e.g. accept + pay cost + apply extra).
- **Log messages.** Activity log reflects cost deduction and extra effects.
- **Loss checks.** If deduction drops coins or reputation to zero, normal loss checks fire.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `cost` or `extraEffect` behave identically to pre-change.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `resolveStorylineOption` applies cost + extra effect.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` logging updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveStorylineOption` and `resolveEventOption`.
- Updated log messages.
- Unit tests for cost/extra effect application.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — straightforward resource mutation.
data.title: Implement cost deduction and extra effects at resolution

# Resolve conditional successors at option resolution time

## Summary

When resolving an option, evaluate `conditionalSuccessors` in order — the first matching rule wins. Fall back to the option's existing `successorId` when no conditions match. This enables branching based on game state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Conditional evaluation.** `conditionalSuccessors` are evaluated sequentially; the first rule whose `{ field, op, value }` matches current `state.resourceBank.{field}` determines the pushed card ID.
- **Fallback.** When no conditions match, the option's `successorId` is used.
- **All boundary cases tested.** Above/below threshold, equality boundary (`==`), and no-match fallback.
- **Successor-card push.** The matched successor is pushed via `pushChainCard` as before.
- **Backwards compatible.** Options without `conditionalSuccessors` push `successorId` as before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Update `resolveStorylineOption` to evaluate conditional successors.

## Deliverables

- Conditional successor evaluation logic.
- Unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNYFJT006PKLC (cost deduction and extra effects).
- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — pure predicate evaluation.

# Update resolveEventOption to use the stored presented option list

## Summary

`resolveEventOption` in `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` currently indexes into `getStorylineOptions(event)` (the full list). Update it to use `pending.presentedOptions` (the affordability-filtered list) so the option index stored at draw time maps correctly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Index into presented list.** `resolveEventOption` resolves using `pending.presentedOptions[optionIndex]` instead of `getStorylineOptions(event)[optionIndex]`.
- **Fallback to full list.** When `presentedOptions` is null/empty, fall back to `getStorylineOptions(event)`.
- **Transcript stability.** The transcript records the chosen option label from the presented list.
- **Backwards compatible.** Legacy events without `presentedOptions` behave identically.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses `pending.presentedOptions`.

## Deliverables

- Updated `resolveEventOption`.
- Unit tests confirming index stability.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURNXOXW007OTLE (affordability filtering).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed.

# Update AI policy to select only among presented/affordable options

## Summary

`decideEventChoice` in `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` currently returns `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta`/`reputationDelta`. Generalise it to select from the presented option list, accounting for cost and extra-effect deltas when projecting outcomes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AI selects from presented options.** The AI considers only options in the presented list (already filtered by affordability).
- **Cost-aware projection.** When projecting outcomes, the AI accounts for `cost` and `extraEffect` in addition to `effectPolicy` effects.
- **Regression harness passes.** The Monte Carlo and regression harnesses run to completion without AI stalls or invalid selections.
- **Backwards compatible.** For legacy binary-choice events, AI behaviour is identical to before.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` generalised for multi-way affordability-aware selection.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolvePendingEventChoice` wiring updated.

## Deliverables

- Updated AI policy.
- Regression/Monte Carlo harness tests green.
- Unit tests for AI policy with cost-gated options.

## Dependencies

- MS-0MURO0VB30076NSE (engine turn closing update).
- MS-0MURNYFJT006PKLC (cost deduction and extra effects).
- MS-0MURNZWHY003TMBC (conditional successor resolution).
- MS-0MURNSK7B004FVZR (model extension).

## Prototype/Experiment

None needed — deterministic scoring policy.

# Extend storyline validator and schema to cover cost, extraEffect, conditionalSuccessors

## Summary

Update the static validator (`src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`) and the JSON schema (`schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`) to understand and validate the new optional fields. Reject invalid data (negative costs, unknown fields/ops, dangling conditional successors).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Cost validation.** Reject negative or zero costs.
- **Condition validation.** Reject conditions with unknown `field` or `op`; reject non-numeric `value`.
- **Extra effect validation.** Reject negative extra effect values.
- **Conditional successor validation.** Reject dangling conditional successors.
- **Shipped content validates cleanly.** All shipped CSVs produce valid storylines.
- **Schema updated.** JSON schema accepts the new optional fields.
- **Doc-drift test passes.**

## Key Files

- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — Add validation rules for new fields.

# Farm to Table is too OP

**Headline.** Retune the `evt-farm-table` (Farm-to-Table Feature) Incident
reward from **600 coins / 100 reputation** to **400 coins / 65 reputation**
(a reduction of at least one third, rounded to the nearest 5), keeping the
Restaurant Renaissance escalation strictly better than its trigger, and
validate the change against the canonical balance guardrails.

## Problem statement

The Farm-to-Table Feature Incident (`evt-farm-table`), the terminal positive
escalation of the Restaurant Renaissance storyline, awards a flat 600 coins and
100 reputation. That windfall is large enough to distort the turn economy and
makes the escalation disproportionately valuable relative to every other
Incident, including its own trigger. The producer wants the reward reduced by
at least one third.

## Users

- **Producer / balance owner** — wants positive Incident rewards that do not
  overwhelm the business economy or trivialise a run; needs an evidence-led
  retune with guardrail validation.
- **Player** — should experience Farm-to-Table as a meaningful but not
  game-deciding reward for rejecting the Popular Menu Item branch.

Example user story: *As a player who rejects Popular Menu Item and escalates
to Farm-to-Table Feature, I want a reward that feels better than the trigger
without trivialising the run.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Reward retuned.** The `evt-farm-table` row in `src/card-data.csv` has
   `coinDelta = 400` and `reputationDelta = 65` (a ≥ one-third reduction from
   600/100, rounded to the nearest 5), and its `description` / `effect` text
   states the new values.
2. **Escalation invariant preserved.** The Restaurant Renaissance escalation
   remains strictly better than its trigger — `evt-farm-table`
   (`400 + 65 = 465`) > `evt-popular-menu` (`300 + 0 = 300`) — and
   `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts` passes (with an explicit value
   assertion added or updated).
3. **Generated artefacts regenerated and consistent.** `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`
   is regenerated from the CSV (`npm run storylines:graph`) and the card SVG
   plus `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` are
   regenerated (`node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`); the
   storyline drift test and card-manifest test pass.
4. **Balance guardrail evidence.** A canonical 200-seed greedy Monte Carlo run
   is performed and compared against the committed baseline via the drift
   report; the result (including the card's draw frequency and whether any
   move is within noise) and rationale are recorded in a balance evidence note
   under `docs/main-street/`. The committed baseline is **not** regenerated
   without producer approval.
5. **Documentation and tests.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
   the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Data is source of truth.** All changes are card-data changes (CSV);
  no engine-rule changes.
- **Integer economy.** Coin/reputation values are whole integers, rounded to
  the nearest 5.
- **Chain structure preserved.** `evt-farm-table` remains a terminal,
  choice-less, plain positive Incident; ids and chain links are unchanged.
- **Baseline governance.** Per the balance-guardrail drift workflow, do not
  silently regenerate `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`; report
  drift and seek producer approval before any baseline update.
- **Scope discipline.** No other card or storyline is retuned here; any further
  balance concerns become separate work items.

## Existing state

- `evt-farm-table` row in `src/card-data.csv`: `family=event`,
  `trigger=Incident`, `target=All`, `tier=5`, `coinDelta=600`,
  `reputationDelta=100`, `description` / `effect` = "Farm-to-table features
  earn 600 coins and 100 reputation.", `storylineId=storyline-restaurant`,
  terminal (no accept/reject links).
- Trigger `evt-popular-menu`: `+300` coins, `0` reputation, `hasChoices=true`,
  reject → `evt-farm-table` (accept ends the chain).
- `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts` asserts the rejected escalation is
  strictly better than the trigger.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` is drift-tested byte-for-byte
  against `src/card-data.csv` (`tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` holds generated card SVGs and
  `csv-checksum.json`; the runtime (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign`)
  compares that file's checksum with the bundled `CSV_CHECKSUM`.

## Desired change

Reduce the flat Farm-to-Table reward to 400 coins / 65 reputation, update the
card's effect/description text, regenerate the derived artefacts, and record
the balance-guardrail evidence.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — `evt-farm-table` row: `coinDelta` 600 → 400,
  `reputationDelta` 100 → 65, and the `description` / `effect` strings.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — regenerate via
  `npm run storylines:graph` (drift-tested artefact).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` and the
  `evt-farm-table` SVG — regenerate via
  `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`.
- `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — update the stale `+600` upper-bound
  comment/reference.
- `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts` — keep/extend the explicit
  escalation value assertion.
- `docs/main-street/analysis/` — new balance evidence note (drift report +
  rationale), following the pattern of `community-space-event-repricing.md`.

## Related work

- **MS-0MTT7FC7A000AA58 — Content: New chain cards and retro-fitting**
  (completed): introduced the Restaurant Renaissance chain and its reward
  levels.
- **MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns and
  economy re-tune** (completed): parent economy campaign; this card's value is
  read relative to the slower payback profile.
- **MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5 — Re-price community spaces and events relative to
  slower business payback** (task): direct precedent for an evidence-led
  incident/event reward retune, including Monte Carlo guardrail validation.
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE — Re-tune reputation sources for the slower-coin
  economy** (task): precedent for treating reputation as a balance lever.
- A `find-related` automated report (work items and repo file matches) is
  maintained on the work item description.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption.** "divide by at least 1/3rd" means *reduce by at least one
  third* (producer confirmed option A); rounding 66.67 down to 65 keeps the
  reduction ≥ one third.
- **Assumption.** The reputation reward scales with the coin reward (producer
  confirmed option A).
- **Risk.** A single low-frequency card may not move the Monte Carlo metrics
  beyond noise; the evidence note must state draw frequency and confidence
  rather than implying a measurable win-rate effect.
- **Risk.** Editing the CSV without regenerating `storyline-manifest.json`
  fails the byte-for-byte drift test; editing without regenerating the SVG
  checksum desyncs the runtime card-art regeneration path.
- **Risk (scope creep).** Other storylines/incidents may also read as
  overpowered; record those as separate work items rather than expanding this
  one.
- **Assumption.** No engine-rule change is needed — the reward is a flat
  `target=All` delta applied once.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should the reward be retuned?**
  Options: (A) reduce *by* at least 1/3 → 400 / 66 rep; (B) reduce *to* one
  third → 200 / 33 rep; (C) other.
  **Recommended:** A.
  — **Answer (producer):** "A but round to nearest 5" → **400 coins / 65
  reputation**. Source: interactive reply. Resolves the conflict with the
  `chain-content.test.ts` escalation invariant (465 > 300).
- **Q2 — Scale the reputation reward too?**
  Options: (A) scale both; (B) coins only; (C) reputation only.
  **Recommended:** A.
  — **Answer (producer):** "A". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Validation scope (balance change)?**
  Options: (A) canonical 200-seed greedy Monte Carlo guardrail run + evidence
  note; (B) data + unit/doc updates only.
  **Recommended:** A.
  — **Answer (producer):** "A". Source: interactive reply.

Open questions: none.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0** – Some staff cards should add action points (completed)
- **MS-0MURODBVT007ZJLT** – Add docs-path-drift.test.ts Vitest drift guard (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, added, also, analysis (+241 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: 0muq50i1y000b6l3, accept, added, analysis, answer (+193 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, added, also, analysis (+189 more)

## Goal
As a Main Street player, I want installed entitled packs' cards dealt into my game and restored on load, so new content is persistent and save-compatible.

Cross-repo child of Tableau-Card-Engine CG-0MUZIS410002Z8EH (epic CG-0MUZFD1WR0031QTB, DLC support for card packs). The core contract/loader/merge landed in the engine (F1-F7); this item is the Main Street consumer.

## Acceptance Criteria
- src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts resolves active packs through the core loader/client and feeds base CARD_DATA_RAW + pack rows through the core merge into a single loadTemplatesFromCsv entry point; pack cards deal and appear in play.
- Saves persist the active pack ids + versions + the merged checksum; load restores the same pool.
- A missing or disabled pack degrades gracefully: warn, continue with base content, and refuse only when a live card instance requires a missing template.
- No scattered ad-hoc merges: there is one documented merge entry point.
- Cross-repo changes are committed and pushed to the game repo's dev branch and recorded in the Main Street Worklog store.

## Minimal Implementation
- New src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts; extend MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts and MainStreetStateSerialize.ts; bump the ./core submodule to the engine commit carrying the card-pack merge/loader.

## Test Plan
- Unit (Main Street repo): base+pack merge, template accessors, save/load round-trip, missing-pack degradation.
